solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rough diamonds in Parisian street

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means its letters are placed inside the other's

parts.note: rue is the French word for street
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: Uncut stones turning up in a street in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough diamonds' reads as one phrase, but 'Rough' alone is the definition and D sits inside RUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude can mean crude or roughly made, as in a rude shelter, so it matches rough.

clue.text: Two different pandas? One huge star!

wordplay.note: the red panda and the giant panda are two distinct species

explanation.surface: Spotting two kinds of panda, one of them a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: The two panda species lend their first words; 'star' then switches from celebrity to astronomy.
explanation.definitionFit: A red giant is a large, cool, late-stage star that has swollen to an enormous size.

clue.text: Reactionary person in two parties

wordplay.note: a do is a party, and two of them are joined

explanation.surface: A political die-hard who belongs to two parties at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodo is used figuratively for someone hopelessly old-fashioned, after the extinct bird.

clue.text: Standard fit for moral tale

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level
fit to do something is able to do it

explanation.surface: Something deemed a suitable norm for a story with a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: A parable is a simple story told to illustrate a moral or religious lesson.

clue.text: Fear of ale that's not real, might some say?

indicators.note: what some might say is spoken, so the answer is how the words are heard

parts.note: faux is French for false, and ale is a beer

explanation.surface: A drinker dreads fake beer as opposed to proper real ale.
explanation.walkthrough: Real ale is the British term for traditionally brewed cask beer, which makes the surface sound like a pub grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A phobia is an extreme or irrational fear of something.

clue.text: Nothing sinister about this trusted adviser?

definitions.text: Nothing sinister about this trusted adviser?

parts.words: Nothing sinister about this trusted adviser?
parts.note: surface reading: a loyal adviser with no evil intent
setter's reading: sinister is Latin for left, so nothing left-handed about him

explanation.walkthrough: Sinister means left in Latin and heraldry, so an adviser with nothing sinister is on the other side.
explanation.definitionFit: A right-hand man is someone's chief assistant and most trusted helper.

clue.text: Sheepish sound from Liberal in heavy defeat

indicators.note: one thing inside another means its letter is placed within the other word

parts.note: a beating is a heavy defeat
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A meek complaint from a Liberal politician after an election rout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sheepish' suggests embarrassment; here it literally means sheep-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleating is the cry a sheep makes, and also feeble complaining.

clue.text: Enjoyment found in cathouse as ever

indicators.note: something found in words sits within them, spanning their letters

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Pleasure to be had at a brothel, as always.
explanation.walkthrough: A cathouse is slang for a brothel.
explanation.definitionFit: Ease can mean comfort and freedom from worry, a relaxed enjoyment of life.

clue.text: Power in hooch in yard possibly causing neurosis

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so the letters may be rearranged

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for power in physics
taken as written

explanation.surface: Strong moonshine drunk in a backyard might bring on mental trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Hooch is cheap or illicit liquor; the second 'in' belongs to the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypochondria is a chronic anxiety about one's health, classed as a neurosis.

clue.text: Insect eggs land oddly when thrown

indicators.note: things thrown land scattered in a jumble, so the preceding letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Eggs flung about come down in a strange way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the letters; the signal is 'when thrown'.
explanation.definitionFit: Daddy-long-legs is the common name for the crane fly, a gangly flying insect.

clue.text: Japanese band seen in Bielsko-Biala

indicators.note: something seen in a place is visible inside it, so look within the following words

parts.note: spans the end of the first part and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A Japanese band spotted on tour in a Polish city.
explanation.walkthrough: Bielsko-Biala is a city in southern Poland, so 'band' looks musical; here it is a strip of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: An obi is the broad sash worn around the waist with a Japanese kimono.

clue.text: Top story in America?

parts.note: surface reading: the leading news item in the United States
setter's reading: the highest floor of a house, spelt story in American usage

explanation.walkthrough: 'Top story' sounds like a headline; Americans spell storey (a floor) as story, which the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: The attic is the room or space at the very top of a house, just under the roof.

clue.text: Barrel with good gun metal

parts.note: a tun is a large cask or barrel
G is the abbreviation for good
the Sten is a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: A firearm with a fine barrel made of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tungsten is a hard, heavy metallic element used in filaments and tools.

clue.text: Unbeliever witnessing bank job?

parts.note: to be at an event is to be present there and see it
a heist is a robbery, such as of a bank

explanation.surface: Someone who doubts what they saw during a bank robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the whimsical split: a person 'at heist' is watching a robbery.
explanation.definitionFit: An atheist is a person who does not believe in the existence of any god.

clue.text: Winding tramline comes to depot

indicators.note: a winding route twists about, so the letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A twisting tram route ends at the depot.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminal is the end station or depot where a transport line finishes.

clue.text: Slender urchin's first encountered in Euston, straying

indicators.note: met inside something means placed within the other letters
straying means wandering from the proper path, so the letters wander out of order

parts.note: taken as written; Euston is a London railway station

indicators.note: the first of a word means only its opening letter is used

parts.note: opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A thin street child is met wandering around a London station.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenuous means very thin or slight, as in a tenuous thread, so it fits slender.

clue.text: Gutless swine about to plagiarise writer

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the outer letters go around the other word
without its guts a word loses its inside, keeping only its two ends

parts.note: the first and last letters
to crib is to copy someone else's work

explanation.surface: A cowardly rotter is going to steal from an author.
explanation.definitionFit: A scribe is someone who writes, especially a copyist of manuscripts or a journalist.

clue.text: Reign disrupted in African republic

indicators.note: something disrupted is thrown out of order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A ruler's time in power interrupted in an African country.
explanation.definitionFit: Niger is a landlocked republic in West Africa, named after the river.

clue.text: Fish and chips one decides to start with

indicators.note: to start with points to the opening letter of each of the words before it

parts.note: the opening letter of each word

explanation.surface: Choosing what fish to have with your chips at the chippy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish and chips' reads as one dish, but 'Fish' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cod is a common edible sea fish, the classic choice in a British fish supper.

clue.text: Hero unemployed reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as told by others, so the answer is how the word is heard

parts.note: someone unemployed is idle

explanation.surface: A news item that a celebrated person is out of work.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is someone greatly admired, a hero to their fans.

clue.text: Prima donna keen to make comeback

indicators.note: a comeback goes back the way it came, so the word is read in the other direction

parts.note: avid means keen

explanation.surface: An opera star eager to return to the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a celebrated female opera singer, the same as a prima donna.

clue.text: Drive to discourage race on M1

parts.note: to deter is to discourage
the digit 1 stands for the letter I
a race or people is a nation

explanation.surface: Trying to stop people speeding on Britain's main motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; 'on' places the second piece after it in this across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Drive as a noun means resolute energy and persistence, which is what determination is.

clue.text: Rope and long time needed for descent

parts.note: a line is a rope or cord
an age is a very long period

explanation.surface: Climbing gear and patience required for going down a cliff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'descent' suggests abseiling down; here it means ancestry.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineage is line of ancestry, and descent in this sense means family origin.

clue.text: Googly say bowled everyone!

parts.note: B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A cricketer cheers a deceptive delivery that dismissed the whole side.
explanation.walkthrough: A googly is a cricket delivery from a leg-spinner that turns the unexpected way; 'say' marks it as one example of a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket each delivery is called a ball, and a googly is one particular kind.
